newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS Cargo says freight traffic up 16 pct Jan-May.
newsitem.headline: SAS Cargo says freight traffic up 16 pct Jan-May.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS said on Tuesday it handled 106,290 tonnes of cargo in the first five months of 1997, a rise of 16 percent over the same 1996 period.
SAS said in a statement a cancellation of four of its weekly passenger flights to Osaka in February and March had been offset by an increase in its volumes on intercontinental routes.
SAS has operated a Boeing 747-200 freighter since March 1996 which flies once weekly to the United States and twice per week to Osaka and Macau.
"The Japanese market as well as freight on the routes to and from Delhi and Bangkok and Newark have been on the positive side," SAS Cargo said.

The airline said it had increased its cargo capacity to Hong Kong through a higher frequency of weekly passenger flights since April, four instead of five. It also added a new five times weekly night flight between Copenhagen and Newark.
Because of this, SAS Cargo said it would have good potential to improve current market development.
"SAS Cargo for example will have approximately 400 tonnes per week of available capacity between Scandinavia and Newark on its passenger flights," it said.

Its freighter operation accounts for a substantial part of the increase in traffic volumes, the airlines said. SAS Cargo's market share rose both to and from Japan and the United States since the start of the all-cargo flights, SAS said.
SAS said freight from Hong Kong to Scandinavia was the most reliable source for filling the freighter to close to 100 percent on each departure.
The airline had stepped up its sales force in Japan and it was now reponsible for selling approximately 30 percent of the capacity from Osaka.
